title: cam sidecar --help starts the daemon (no --help guard); undocumented deterministic flags across commands
description: Safety bug hit live 2026-07-07: cam sidecar --help does NOT print usage, it STARTS the long-lived sidecar daemon (the arg is ignored, the daemon boots) — a stray sidecar spawned and had to be killed by hand. cam sidecar is also absent from cam --help (internal command, undiscoverable). Separately, real deterministic flags are undocumented in their command --help: cam issue --file-local (the commit-to-main filer used by the orchestrator), the cam journal append stdin-JSON schema, and the cam issue close/abandon that CAM-210 will add. Fix: (1) add a --help/-h short-circuit guard to EVERY command incl. internal ones (print usage, exit 0, NEVER start a daemon or mutate on --help); (2) document the deterministic stdin-JSON / --file-local flags in each command --help; (3) list internal commands (sidecar) in cam --help or mark them explicitly internal. Concrete Layer-1 instance of CAM-197 (discoverable + safe deterministic CLI). Origin: operator noticed a --help that did not work + the stray-sidecar incident during CAM-201, 2026-07-07.

acceptanceCriteria: A central --help/-h short-circuit at the dispatch/arg-parse layer prints usage and exits 0 BEFORE any command side-effect runs, covering every registered command including internal ones.
cam sidecar --help prints usage and exits 0 WITHOUT starting the sidecar daemon.
--help/-h never starts a daemon and never mutates state, in any command.
A table-driven test iterates every registered command and asserts --help exits 0 with no side-effect (no daemon spawn, no filesystem/state mutation).
cam --help lists internal commands (sidecar) under an explicit Internal section, marked as internal rather than user-facing entry points.
Each relevant command --help documents its deterministic flags: cam issue --file-local, the cam journal append stdin-JSON schema, and cam issue close/abandon.
bun run check:all passes and bun test is green.
spec.scope: IN: the central --help/-h short-circuit guard at the dispatch layer; the Internal section in cam --help; per-command usage text documenting the deterministic flags (issue --file-local, journal append stdin JSON, issue close/abandon); a table-driven help-safety test across all registered commands. OUT: the broader CAM-197 epic (this is one concrete Layer-1 slice); any behavior change to the commands themselves beyond the help short-circuit; adding new deterministic flags (they already exist, this only documents them).
gotchas: The live bug: cam sidecar ignores the unknown --help arg and boots the long-lived daemon (a stray sidecar had to be killed by hand). The guard MUST intercept before the command body runs, not inside each command body.
Internal commands (sidecar) are currently absent from cam --help and thus undiscoverable; the fix adds them under an Internal section without implying they are user-facing entry points.
The deterministic flags being documented (--file-local, journal append stdin JSON, close/abandon) already exist as behavior; this criterion documents them in --help, it does not add them.
A per-command guard is a band-aid that re-opens the footgun for every new command; the central dispatch-layer guard is the root-cause fix and is what the table-driven test protects.
